title: Displaying Owned NFTs Using the React Router
section: 42. Minting NFTs and Building an NFT Marketplace like OpenSea
summary: Adds client-side navigation to OpenD with react-router-dom (Home, Discover, Minter, My NFTs) and gives the backend memory of what was minted: two HashMaps record every NFT and each owner's list of NFT ids. A new getOwnedNFTs query returns the ids, and the My NFTs route maps them into a Gallery of Item components.

concepts.heading: Why routing is needed
points: After minting, the user needs a place to see everything they own. The nav buttons (Discover, Minter, My NFTs) are inactive, so react-router-dom (a dependency already listed in package.json, like react-hook-form) is used to switch views by URL path.
Preparation in App.jsx: comment out the temporary Minter and the hard-coded NFT id, so that only Header and Footer remain; the Header will own the routing and page content.

(Extra) The code uses react-router-dom v5 (^5.2.0 in the reference package.json), where Switch exists. In v6 Switch was renamed Routes and routes take an element prop, so the syntax below does not carry over directly.

concepts.heading: BrowserRouter and Link
points: Import { BrowserRouter, Link, Switch, Route } from "react-router-dom" in Header.jsx.
Wrap everything the Header returns in <BrowserRouter>. It provides the routing context that Link and Route require.

Link turns text into a navigation link without a full page request. Its to attribute is the path: /discover, /minter, /collection (the My NFTs collection). Wrap the link around the text inside each button, not around the button itself, and use a different path on each of the three.
Also wrap the OpenD title (the h5) in <Link to="/"> so clicking the logo text returns to the home route.

concepts.heading: Switch and Route
points: Switch inspects the current URL and renders the first Route whose path matches, much like a JavaScript switch statement checking cases from top to bottom. Put it beneath the header markup, still inside BrowserRouter.

Four Route children are needed: home, discover, minter, collection. Each has a path attribute that must match the corresponding Link's to value exactly (copy-paste to avoid typos), and whatever sits between the Route tags is what gets rendered.
Home route (path "/"): the home image, moved out of App.jsx together with its import line (the image import now lives in Header.jsx).

Discover route: only a placeholder

Discover

for now; it will list NFTs for sale once listing is built in later lessons.
Minter route: <Minter />, imported from ./Minter.
Collection route: the Gallery of the user's NFTs (first with a hard-coded Item, then dynamic data, see below).

Matching problem: the path "/" matches every URL, so if it comes first it always wins. Two fixes: move it to the end of the Switch, or (preferred) add the exact attribute so it matches only when the path is exactly "/".

concepts.heading: Making Gallery reusable
points: Gallery was a static grid with one Item. Item breaks without an id (Principal.fromText on undefined), which showed up as a blank My NFTs page; a temporary fix was to give the Item the canister id used earlier.
The heading was hard-coded as Discover. Replace it with {props.title} and pass title="My NFTs" from where Gallery is used, so the same component can serve Discover and My NFTs later.

concepts.heading: Backend: tracking NFTs and owners
points: Until now mint only returned the new canister id and nothing was remembered. The backend needs a data store in main.mo, built with HashMap (import HashMap "mo:base/HashMap").

mapOfNFTs: a var HashMap whose key is the NFT canister's Principal and whose value is the NFTActorClass.NFT instance. Constructed as HashMap.HashMap<Principal, NFTActorClass.NFT>(1, Principal.equal, Principal.hash): the first argument is an initial capacity, then the key-equality function and the key-hash function. After obtaining newNFTPrincipal in mint, call mapOfNFTs.put(newNFTPrincipal, newNFT).

mapOfOwners: key is the owner's Principal, value is a List.List<Principal> of the NFT canister ids that owner holds, because one owner can have many NFTs. Import List (mo:base/List). Same constructor arguments (Principal keys).

A plain put is not enough for mapOfOwners since the existing list must be read, extended and written back. This is done in a separate private func addToOwnershipMap(owner : Principal, nftId : Principal). private keeps it unreachable from outside the actor.

Inside it: mapOfOwners.get(owner) returns an option (?List), because a first-time owner has no entry. Resolve it with a switch expression wrapped in parentheses: case null returns an empty list via List.nil<Principal>(); case (?result) returns the unwrapped result. Declaring the variable's type as List.List<Principal> is what makes the compiler complain until the option is unwrapped.

Then ownedNFTs := List.push(nftId, ownedNFTs); (push puts the new element at the head and returns the new list, so the variable must be reassigned with :=), followed by mapOfOwners.put(owner, ownedNFTs).
Call addToOwnershipMap(owner, newNFTPrincipal) from mint after the mapOfNFTs.put.
The lecture mentions a naming typo in the earlier return (variable name mismatch) that happened not to cause an error; keep newNFTPrincipal consistent.

concepts.heading: Backend: query for a user's NFTs (exercise)
points: Add public query func getOwnedNFTs(user : Principal) : async [Principal]. A pause-and-try moment: repeat the same get-and-unwrap switch used above.

Declare var userNFTs : List.List<Principal> = switch (mapOfOwners.get(user)) { case null List.nil<Principal>(); case (?result) result }; then return List.toArray(userNFTs) to convert the list into an array, the type sent to the frontend as a JS array of Principals.

concepts.heading: Frontend: fetching and rendering the owned NFTs
points: In Header.jsx import the backend actor from ../../../declarations/OPEND_backend and write async function getNFTs() that does const userNFTIds = await OPEND_backend.getOwnedNFTs(CURRENT_USER_ID);. Log it first to check the array.

CURRENT_USER_ID is the anonymous principal ("2vxsx-fae") exported from main.jsx, used so the login flow can be skipped. Import it into Header with the default import from ../main. Both lines defining and exporting it must exist in main.jsx.
Run getNFTs once on first render with useEffect(() => { getNFTs(); }, []); the empty dependency array limits it to a single call.
Redeploy using the README command; after minting a few more NFTs the logged array contains one principal per mint (the lecture's test user had three).

Store a ready-made Gallery element in state: const [userOwnedGallery, setOwnedGallery] = useState(); then in getNFTs call setOwnedGallery(<Gallery title="My NFTs" ids={userNFTIds} />). The collection Route renders {userOwnedGallery}.

Gallery: const [items, setItems] = useState(); a function fetchNFTs that checks props.ids != undefined and then calls setItems(props.ids.map(NFTId => <Item id={NFTId} key={NFTId.toText()} />)). The arrow function returns JSX wrapped in parentheses (not braces) for an implicit return.
React requires a unique key on list-rendered elements; the principal converted with toText() is a convenient unique value (Principal import needed only if used for typing).

Call fetchNFTs inside useEffect with an empty dependency array, and render {items} inside the innermost grid div in the Gallery markup. Items placed outside that div display stacked on separate lines; check the closing div position if the layout looks off.

Item.jsx change: ids from the gallery are Principal objects, not strings, so Item should stop calling Principal.fromText and just use props.id directly. (Extra) In the reference repo Minter still passes nftPrincipal.toText(), a string; the agent's createActor accepts either a string or a Principal for canisterId, so both paths work.

Refresh problem: a freshly minted NFT only appears in My NFTs after a manual page reload, because Header (and its useEffect) ran before the mint. Setting forceRefresh={true} on BrowserRouter makes each Link navigation do a full page reload, re-running the effect so the new NFT shows. (Extra) This is a blunt fix; re-fetching on route change or lifting state up would avoid full reloads.

task.name: Routing plus 'My NFTs' gallery
task.starting_point: Project from 42.04: working Minter, static Gallery with a single Item, inactive nav buttons, main.mo with only a mint function.
task.goal: Clicking the nav items switches between Home, Discover, Minter and My NFTs; My NFTs lists an Item card for every NFT minted by the current (anonymous) user, including newly minted ones.
steps: Comment out Minter and the hard-coded nftId in App.jsx; keep Header and Footer.
In Header.jsx import BrowserRouter, Link, Switch, Route; wrap the returned markup in BrowserRouter.
Wrap the text of each nav button in a Link with to="/discover", "/minter", "/collection", and wrap the OpenD title in a Link to "/".
Add a Switch with four Routes: exact path "/" (home image), "/discover" (h1 placeholder), "/minter" (Minter), "/collection" (Gallery). Move the home image and its import from App into the Route.
Make Gallery accept props.title and pass title="My NFTs".
In main.mo add mapOfNFTs and mapOfOwners HashMaps, populate mapOfNFTs in mint, and write private addToOwnershipMap with the option-unwrapping switch and List.push; call it from mint.
Write public query func getOwnedNFTs(user : Principal) : async [Principal] returning List.toArray of the user's list (empty list when the user is unknown).

In Header.jsx call getOwnedNFTs(CURRENT_USER_ID) inside an async function triggered by useEffect with an empty array; store <Gallery title="My NFTs" ids={...} /> in useState and render it in the collection Route.
In Gallery.jsx map props.ids to <Item id={...} key={...toText()} /> via state and useEffect and render the result inside the grid container.
Update Item.jsx to use props.id directly (a Principal) instead of parsing text.
Redeploy, mint several NFTs, open My NFTs; add forceRefresh={true} to BrowserRouter so new NFTs appear without a manual reload.
task.expected_result: Header links change the displayed page. Home shows the landing image, Discover shows a heading, Minter shows the minting form, My NFTs shows a grid of cards (image, name, owner) for every NFT the anonymous user has minted, with the newest first because List.push adds at the head.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 42 - Minting NFTs and Building an NFT Marketplace like OpenSea/42.05 Displaying Owned NFTs Using the React Router/OPEND/src (OPEND_backend/main.mo, OPEND_frontend/src/components/Header.jsx, Gallery.jsx, Item.jsx)

pitfalls: Putting the Link around the button instead of the text, or giving two buttons the same path.
Link to values not matching Route paths exactly, for example a typo or capitalisation difference.
Leaving the root Route without exact (or not placing it last), so it matches every URL.
Calling Gallery's Item without an id, which crashes rendering and leaves My NFTs blank.
Forgetting that mapOfOwners.get returns an option; assigning it straight to a List type is a compile error.
Forgetting to reassign after List.push (it returns a new list) and to put the result back into the map.
Keeping Principal.fromText in Item while passing Principal objects from the Gallery.
Using curly braces instead of parentheses in the map callback, so no JSX is returned.
Placing {items} outside the grid container div, which breaks the layout.
New mints not appearing until a manual reload unless forceRefresh is set.
(Extra) The reference Gallery calls the state variable itemms (typo); other leftovers such as unused imports in the reference code can be removed.
(Extra) HashMaps declared as transient var in the reference repo (a persistent actor) are cleared on every canister upgrade; deployments that reinstall the code lose the ownership data.

gaps_and_ideas: Proposed lesson: 'Client-side routing with react-router-dom v5 (Link, Switch, Route)'. Blurb: build a four-page mini app whose nav links change the rendered component without reloading.

Tasks: (1) wrap a nav in BrowserRouter and add three Links; (2) add a Switch with Routes for each path; (3) observe the bug when the '/' route lacks exact, then fix it; (4) make a reusable Gallery that takes title and an ids array and renders items with map and a unique key; (5) add a list-of-owned-items state that updates when a 'mint' button is pressed.
Starter code: a Header with three plain buttons and a Gallery with a hard-coded card.

Interactive demo: a URL bar simulator showing which Route matches in order, toggling exact on and off, plus a fake owner-to-items map (as a JS Map of arrays) that mirrors the Motoko mapOfOwners and shows the get/unwrap/push/put sequence step by step.
